pairs.finding_text: Although comparisons to prior DRL methods are mentioned, no explicit description of competitive baselines or state-of-the-art benchmarking protocol is provided in the experimental section. The paper references prior work ([29; 30]) and states that comparisons are performed, but the experimental setup does not clearly describe which baselines are implemented, how they are configured, or whether official results are used. Without a transparent and comprehensive SOTA comparison protocol, it is difficult to assess the claimed performance gains. Clear benchmarking against recognized state-of-the-art methods is essential for positioning the contribution. Explicitly list all baseline methods, their implementation details, and whether official code or reported results are used. Provide a comparison table including state-of-the-art DRL and non-DRL methods with consistent evaluation metrics and instance settings.
pairs.unit_text: This raises concerns about the comprehensiveness of the evaluation and potentially limits the generalizability of the proposed method's performance.
pairs.reason: F: baselines not described or benchmarked transparently; U: evaluation not comprehensive. Documentation vs breadth.

pairs.finding_text: Critical training details for Dueling DQN are missing: learning rate, optimizer, discount factor, replay buffer size, batch size, target network update strategy, epsilon-greedy schedule, and number of training steps per episode. DQN-based methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameters and training schedules. Without these details, the method is not reproducible and reported performance cannot be independently validated. Add a dedicated implementation details subsection listing all hyperparameters, network architectures (layer sizes, activation functions), exploration strategy, target network update frequency, replay buffer configuration, hardware used, and training time.
pairs.unit_text: The method is evaluated only two public benchmarks, whereas the DRL baseline [1] has been tested on a more extensive set of benchmarks.
pairs.reason: F: missing DQN hyperparameters; U: evaluated on only two benchmarks.

pairs.finding_text: During improvement, multiple solutions (n_t) are generated and the one with minimal makespan is selected. This introduces a selection bias that effectively performs a greedy best-of-n search within each step, but its computational cost and fairness relative to baselines are not analyzed. If the method internally evaluates multiple candidate solutions per step and keeps the best, comparisons to baselines that produce a single trajectory may be unfair unless computational budgets are matched. It also affects the interpretation of the RL signal. Report the average n_t per step, total number of solution evaluations per instance, and compare against baselines under equal computational budgets. Analyze whether performance gains persist when limiting to a single improvement attempt.
pairs.unit_text: Note that in Section 3.2 “Policy Model” (P6), there is no way to understand the description “Obviously, there are at most m different insertion schemes for each improvement decision.”
pairs.reason: F: best-of-n selection bias; U: an unclear sentence about insertion schemes.

Without comparison to established neural improvement paradigms, this appears as an incremental variant rather than a broadly new paradigm.
